I added **3 distinct E2E tests** in [onboarding.e2e.ts](/Users/timhorgas/git/Youmotion/e2e/appduct/onboarding.e2e.ts):

1. Open Pulse after skipping onboarding.
2. Open Settings and return to Pulse.
3. Confirm onboarding stays skipped after restarting.

Each runs on iOS and Android: **6 platform/test combinations, all passing on the final runs**. Including debugging, I ran **13 suites × 3 tests = 39 test attempts**. The **468 tests** mentioned earlier are the Jest suite, not E2E.

Their value is proving that the real app, navigation actor, native database and UI work together. Every test starts fresh, verifies onboarding is incomplete, skips it twice to check idempotency, loads the synthetic archive, and verifies persisted completion after restart. Coverage is still narrow: these are smoke tests, not comprehensive product coverage.

The framework’s differentiator is combining ordinary locator/assertion tests with optional natural-language agent actions that can be recorded and replayed without further model calls. It supports web and mobile through a shared testing API. **Our tests currently use deterministic actions only—no AI calls or credentials.** [Framework documentation](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e)

My assessment: **the strongest benefit we demonstrated is Appduct’s reliable setup shortcut**, rather than a unique advantage of this runner. The runner gives us reusable cross-platform tests and reports, but we haven’t established that it beats Maestro, Detox or Harness for Youmotion. It is also pre-1.0, with changing APIs. I’d keep this small suite as a pilot before making it our main E2E framework. [Project status](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e#status)
